findings.title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query after deleting cache
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx` does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess` or `onSettled` (unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it on line 62). Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` often renders without an `onChanged` callback that refetches connected calendars, `connectedCalendar.cacheUpdatedAt` remains stale in the React Query cache after the user deletes the cache, so the dropdown continues showing the old "Cache Status" and "Delete cached data" action until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: `credentialIds` can contain `null` or `undefined`, causing Prisma validation errors in `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`
findings.body: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` is passed directly to `cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, which executes `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })`. On `CalendarCache`, `credentialId` is a non-nullable `Int`, whereas `connectedCalendar.credentialId` can be `null` or `undefined` (for example on broken/delegation credentials). Passing `null`/`undefined` inside the `in` array to Prisma for a non-nullable column throws a `PrismaClientValidationError` at runtime and breaks the `connectedCalendars` query. Filter `credentialIds` with `.filter((id): id is number => typeof id === "number")` before querying.
